name: Cortana
description: Voice assistant, demoted and largely unused since Windows 11. Windows Search is unaffected.

name: Bing Weather
description: Weather app. The taskbar widget already shows the forecast.

name: Bing News
description: Bing news feed, replaced by Microsoft Start on newer installs.

name: Microsoft Start
description: Search and news panel bundled with Windows 11.

name: Windows Maps
description: Offline-capable maps app. A browser covers the same ground.

name: Mail and Calendar
description: The classic Mail and Calendar client, superseded by the new Outlook.

name: Feedback Hub
description: Bug reports and feedback to Microsoft. Needed only for the Insider programme.

name: Get Help
description: Support app that opens a Microsoft help channel.

name: Get Started
description: The tips app Windows shows after a fresh install.

name: Mixed Reality Portal
description: Launcher for Windows Mixed Reality headsets.

name: 3D Viewer
description: 3D model viewer bundled with Windows 10.

name: Paint 3D
description: The 3D Paint successor. Removing it leaves classic Paint untouched.

name: Print 3D
description: 3D printing app. Useless without a 3D printer attached.

name: Alarms and Clock
description: Alarms, timers and the world clock.

name: Camera
description: Camera app. Superfluous on a desktop with no webcam.

name: Voice Recorder
description: Basic audio recorder.

name: Sticky Notes
description: Notes synced to a Microsoft account.

name: Microsoft Wallet
description: Tap to Pay infrastructure, rarely used on a desktop.

name: Messaging
description: Leftover from the Windows 10 Mobile era. No longer functional.

name: Family Safety
description: Parental controls and screen time limits.

name: Power Automate
description: Desktop automation aimed at enterprise users.

name: Microsoft To Do
description: Task list app.

name: People
description: Contacts app, once tied to Mail and Calendar. Redundant now.

name: Microsoft Whiteboard
description: Digital whiteboard. Mostly useful on a touchscreen or Surface.

name: Dev Home
description: Developer dashboard from Microsoft.

name: Microsoft Copilot
description: The Copilot assistant app.

name: Phone Link
description: Links an Android phone to Windows for notifications and file transfer.

name: Office Hub
description: A prompt to buy Microsoft 365. Does nothing if you already have Office.

name: OneNote
description: The Store build of OneNote. The desktop version Office installs is separate.

name: OneDrive
description: The Store entry for OneDrive. The desktop sync client is separate and unaffected.

name: Skype
description: Consumer Skype bundled with Windows.

name: Microsoft Teams
description: The personal Teams build, not the work or school client.

name: Clipchamp
description: Video editor bundled since Windows 11 22H2.

name: Groove Music
description: Discontinued music player, still present on older Windows 10 installs.

name: Movies and TV
description: Local video player. VLC or MPC-HC do the same job.

name: Spotify
description: The Store build of Spotify. Separate from a copy installed from the website.

name: Netflix
description: Netflix Store app, sometimes preinstalled by a manufacturer.

name: Xbox Game Bar
description: The Win+G overlay. It can also be switched off in Settings under Gaming.

name: Xbox Identity Provider
description: Sign-in broker for Xbox services and Game Pass.

name: Xbox App Services
description: Shared services for the Xbox apps. Only remove it with the rest of them.

name: Solitaire Collection
description: Klondike, FreeCell and Spider, now ad-supported.

name: Candy Crush Saga
description: Preinstalled Candy Crush. A reset can put it back.

name: Candy Crush Soda Saga
description: The second preinstalled Candy Crush title.

name: TikTok
description: TikTok Store app, preinstalled on some new machines.

name: Facebook
description: Facebook Store app, sometimes bundled by a manufacturer.

name: Instagram
description: Instagram Store app.

name: Twitter
description: Twitter Store app.
